newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: SOCCER-SOUTH AFRICA WIN VITAL AWAY POINT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SOUTH AFRICA WIN VITAL AWAY POINT.

text.p: South Africa won a vital away point in their World Cup qualifier against Zambia on Saturday, forcing a goalless draw.
The African champions now lead the table with four points, while top- seeded Zambia's dreams of a place in France next year might well have gone with the draw.
Zambia had the better of the chances, missing a number from close range.
The closest was a shot by Denis Lota in the 34th minute that cannoned off the South African crossbar.
Lota also missed a close-range header in the second half after a period of intense home pressure but in the closing stages it was South Africa who finished stronger.
Midfielder John Moshoeu miskicked a shot with Zambian goalkeeper Davies Phiri beaten and striker Jerry Sikhosana also wasted two chances.
The result left Zambia with just one point from their first two games in the group.
Both teams play again in early April, South Africa going to Congo and Zambia away at neighbouring Zaire.
